ground_truth_soap:
Subjective:

Chief Complaint (CC)
- Follow-up for right knee pain due to osteoarthritis.

History of Present Illness (HPI)
- A 65-year-old Caucasian female with a 5-year history of right knee osteoarthritis presents for a follow-up. She continues to experience moderate to severe knee pain, swelling, stiffness, and occasional locking of the knee. The symptoms are daily and significantly impact her ability to walk, climb stairs, and rise from a seated position. She reports difficulty sleeping due to pain, although she generally maintains a balanced diet and performs prescribed physical therapy exercises 3 times a week. She uses a cane for short distances and has an overall high health literacy.

Review of Systems (ROS)
- Constitutional: Reports good general health but experiences interrupted sleep due to knee pain.
- Musculoskeletal: Complaints of right knee pain, swelling, stiffness, and occasional locking. No new joint involvement.
- Neurological: No reports of numbness, tingling, or weakness.

Objective:

Vitals:
- Blood pressure: 135/85 mm Hg
- Heart rate: 72 BPM

Physical Exam:
- Inspection of the right knee: Swelling and slight deformity noted.
- Palpation: Tenderness along the joint line.
- Range of Motion: Decreased with crepitus during movement.

Investigation/Test Results:
- Previous X-ray: Joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation in the right knee.
- Blood Work: CBC and BMP within normal limits except for slightly elevated cholesterol levels.

Assessment:
- Unilateral primary osteoarthritis, right knee (ICD-10 M17.11)

Plan:
- Medical Treatment:
  - Administer corticosteroid injection in the right knee today to reduce inflammation and pain.
  - Prescribe Meloxicam 15 mg, once daily, oral, for 30 days to manage pain and inflammation.

- Follow-Up and Monitoring:
  - Follow-up appointment in 6 weeks to evaluate the response to the corticosteroid injection.
  - If symptoms do not improve, discuss further options such as knee arthroscopy or total knee replacement.
  
- Referral:
  - MRI of the right knee to assess the extent of cartilage damage.
  - Referral to Dr. John Smith, Orthopedic Surgeon, for further evaluation and management of right knee osteoarthritis.

- Lifestyle and Non-Pharmacological Interventions:
  - Encourage the continuation of physical therapy and weight management activities.
  - Advise avoidance of high-impact activities, continuing with low-impact exercises.

Patient Agreements:
- The patient understands and agrees with the recommended medical treatment plan, follow-up schedule, and lifestyle modifications.
